documents.title: E20 turbo inspection
documents.content:
## Engine turbo
For the synthetic E20 engine, diagnostic code P0299 indicates low boost pressure. Inspect the intake hoses for splits and check the wastegate actuator before replacing the turbocharger. A leaking hose can produce the same code. Do not call every P0299 event a failed turbocharger. Record the pressure test result before repair.

documents.title: E20 cooling
documents.content:
## Engine cooling
The synthetic E20 cooling checklist identifies thermostat T200 as a service inspection item. A slow warm-up and fluctuating coolant temperature require checking the thermostat and coolant level. Do not open the cooling system while hot. Pressure-test the system for external leaks before replacing parts.

documents.title: GX transmission
documents.content:
## Transmission
The synthetic GX generation may use the AT8 automatic transmission. Delayed engagement after selecting drive is an inspection symptom. Check fluid level and diagnostic code S300 before replacing the shift solenoid. A low fluid level can mimic a solenoid fault. Road-test only after safety checks.

documents.title: GX suspension
documents.content:
## Suspension
A front-end clunk over low-speed bumps calls for inspection of strut mounts and stabilizer links on the synthetic GX. Compare both sides and inspect for play with the vehicle safely supported. Noise alone does not identify a failed strut. Record the specific worn component before replacement.

documents.title: GX electrical inspection
documents.content:
## Electronics
Intermittent warning lights on the synthetic GX require a battery voltage and charging-system test. Voltage below 12.2 V at rest is an inspection trigger, not proof of a failed control module. Check ground connections and alternator output before replacing electronics. Store any fault codes found during diagnosis.

documents.title: Aurora body inspection
documents.content:
## Body
Inspect the synthetic Aurora A1 door seams and lower tailgate edge for paint damage or corrosion. Photograph suspicious seams and compare factory sealant with the opposite side. Surface marks do not prove structural rust. Look for previous repair traces and check drainage openings.

documents.title: GX ABS diagnosis
documents.content:
## Brakes
An ABS warning on synthetic GX may require wheel-speed sensor inspection. Diagnostic code C101 refers to the left-front wheel-speed signal in this fictional corpus. Inspect wiring and connector condition before replacing the sensor. Do not infer brake hydraulic failure solely from a C101 code.

documents.title: E20 service checklist
documents.content:
## Service
For the synthetic E20 engine, investigate persistent cold-start chain rattle by checking oil level and timing-chain tension. A brief sound without corroborating evidence is not a confirmed failure. Document duration and engine temperature. Follow the manufacturer service procedure for any repair.

documents.content:
## Recall
This is a synthetic training example: fictional campaign R42 concerns inspection of a fuel-pump connector on Aurora A1. The remedy in this fixture is connector replacement when corrosion is present. It is not a real recall. Verify any real vehicle by VIN and official manufacturer records instead of this test corpus.

documents.title: Aurora purchase inspection
documents.content:
## Inspection
For the synthetic Aurora A1 pre-purchase inspection, request service records, perform a cold start, scan stored diagnostic codes, and inspect underbody damage. A professional mechanic should inspect safety-critical findings. Combine engine, transmission, suspension, electrical, body, and brake evidence; no single symptom proves a common failure.
